deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'An important new advantage in integration by approximation.' This is a German draft of what became Gauss's 'Methodus nova integralium valores per approximationem inveniendi' (presented 1814, printed 1816). The editorial mark [III 163] points to Werke III, p.163.

(1) Motivation. Cotes' (Newton–Cotes) formulas use n equally spaced ordinates and are exact only up to degree about n. If the abscissae may be unequally spaced, n ordinates can be made exact up to the '2n-th order', i.e. for all polynomials of degree at most 2n-1.

(2) Setup. Seek ∫_{m-Δ}^{m+Δ} X dx. The image writes the lower limit as m−δ; this is clearly meant as m−Δ.
- If the number of nodes is odd, x=m must be a node and the other nodes are symmetric pairs m±aΔ, m±bΔ, m±cΔ, ...
- The values of X at these nodes are A, A′, B, B′, C, C′, ...
- The formula has the form Δ[α(A+A′) + β(B+B′) + γ(C+C′) + ...], plus ΔμM when the count is odd, where M = X(m).

(3) Moment equations [my derivation]. Put x = m + sΔ.
- For X = s^{2k}: the exact integral is 2Δ/(2k+1).
- The formula gives 2Δ(αa^{2k} + βb^{2k} + ...), plus Δμ when k=0.
- Odd powers are integrated exactly by symmetry.
- Hence: α+β+γ+...+μ/2 = 1; αa²+βb²+... = 1/3; αa⁴+... = 1/5; αa⁶+... = 1/7; and so on.
- One takes as many equations as there are unknowns (weights and nodes together).

(4) Results, on the normalized interval [-1,1] scaled by Δ:
- n=1: node m, integral 2MΔ, μ=2 (midpoint rule).
- n=2: nodes m±Δ/√3, integral (A+A′)Δ, α=1.
- n=3: nodes m and m±√(3/5)Δ, integral Δ(5/9(A+A′) + 8/9 M) = (1/9)Δ(5(A+A′)+8M), with α=5/9, μ=8/9.
- n=4: a² = 3/7 − √(24/245) and b² = 3/7 + √(24/245). Weights α = 1/2 + √(5/216) at the inner node and β = 1/2 − √(5/216) at the outer node. Gauss adds the uniform weight formula α = −(35/72)a² + 17/24, valid at either node.
- n=5: nodes 0 and ±√(5/9 ∓ √(40/567)). Weights α = 161/450 + (13/900)√70 (inner), β = 161/450 − (13/900)√70 (outer), μ = 128/225. Gauss gives the weight as a polynomial in the node: α = −(7/40)a⁴ − (469/1800)a² + 128/225.
- [Mine] Eliminating a⁴ with the node equation a⁴ = (10/9)a² − 5/21 gives α = −(91/200)a² + 1099/1800, which is Gauss's second form.

(5) General statement, begun here and continued on p.13. For n nodes write x = m − tΔ. Then t runs over ±a, ±b, ... (and 0 when n is odd), and these t are the roots of a polynomial T. On the next page T is given as t^n·₂F₁(...; t^{-2}), i.e. the monic Legendre polynomial P_n.
errors: The lower limit is written m−δ (lowercase) but must be m−Δ; this is a notational slip.
The text says 'Coordinaten' where 'Ordinaten' is meant; this is a verbal slip.
The machine transcription's '1/18 Δ(5/9(A+A′)+8/9 M)' is wrong in any case. The correct expression is Δ(5/9(A+A′)+8/9 M), equivalently (1/9)Δ(5(A+A′)+8M). Gauss's own α=5/9, μ=8/9 is correct.
No mathematical errors were found. All nodes and weights for n=1..5 agree with the Gauss–Legendre values, and both polynomial weight formulas check out (verified numerically).

results.what: Optimal unequal nodes give exactness to degree 2n−1 with n ordinates, versus about degree n for Cotes. The moment equations for symmetric nodes and weights are set up.
Explicit nodes and weights for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in closed radical form.
results.modern_name: Gauss–Legendre nodes and weights (roots of P_n)

results.what: Weights expressed as polynomials in the node: α = 17/24 − (35/72)a² for n=4, and α = 1099/1800 − (91/200)a² for n=5.
results.modern_name: Weight as a polynomial function of the node, reduced modulo P_n (cf. Christoffel-number formulas)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss 1814 (in Methodus nova), later Jacobi/Christoffel for general formulas

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Gauss's own famous 1814 quadrature paper, and the editorial mark points to Werke III p.163. The results are well known and correctly attributed to him. Only minor drafting details, such as the polynomial-in-node weight formulas, could be of interest.

checkable.asserts: One-point rule with μ=2 is exact for constants.
Three-point rule (α=5/9, a²=3/5) satisfies the a⁴ moment: 2·α·a⁴ = 2/5 [the moment equation multiplied by 2].
The monic P4 has roots t² = 3/7 ± √(24/245).
a² = 3/7 − √(24/245) is a root of the quartic in a².
The four-point weight formula α = −35/72·a² + 17/24 gives 1/2+√(5/216) at the inner node.

checkable.sympy: a2=Rational(3,7)-sqrt(Rational(24,245)); b2=Rational(3,7)+sqrt(Rational(24,245)); al=Rational(1,2)+sqrt(Rational(5,216)); be=Rational(1,2)-sqrt(Rational(5,216)); [simplify(al*a2**k+be*b2**k-Rational(1,2*k+1)) for k in range(4)]==[0,0,0,0]
checkable.asserts: The four-point rule satisfies the moment equations up to a⁶ = 1/7.

checkable.sympy: a2=Rational(5,9)-sqrt(Rational(40,567)); b2=Rational(5,9)+sqrt(Rational(40,567)); al=Rational(161,450)+Rational(13,900)*sqrt(70); be=Rational(161,450)-Rational(13,900)*sqrt(70); mu=Rational(128,225); [simplify(al*a2**k+be*b2**k+(mu/2 if k==0 else 0)-Rational(1,2*k+1)) for k in range(5)]==[0,0,0,0,0]
checkable.asserts: The five-point nodes and weights satisfy the moment equations through a⁸ = 1/9.
Gauss's first five-point weight formula is correct at the inner node.
The reduced five-point weight formula is correct at the outer node.

transcription_corrections: The integration limits should read x = m−Δ, x = m+Δ (the image's lowercase δ is a slip for Δ).
Three-point integral: read (1/9)Δ(5(A+A′)+8M), equivalently Δ(5/9(A+A′)+8/9 M); '1/18' is a misreading.
The bold 𝔟 is Gauss's Greek β (beta), the weight for the b-nodes.
The marginal 'wenn μ ausgeschlossen' more plausibly reads 'wenn a⁴ ausgeschlossen'. The second form results from eliminating a⁴ via a⁴ = (10/9)a² − 5/21.
In the five-point line the value read as '128' (μ = 128/225) is correct.
